title: Derived tensor computation through canonical constant-scalar restriction
statement: Let T be a scheme in universe u, Lambda a commutative ring in universe u+1, R its constant commutative ring sheaf, K a K-flat complex of sheaves of R-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], and M a sheaf of R-modules. Let rho be the canonical constant-scalar restriction [lem-kun-tor-model-restriction]. Then Q(rho(Tot(K tensor single(M)))) is isomorphic to the fixed etale derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] of Q(rho K) with single(rho M). The comparison uses the given ring-sheaf tensor and the existing module-valued derived tensor, with no new choice of tensor structure or derived functor.

source.place: Tags 06YH and 0F1M, K-flat computation of derived tensor; constant scalar encoding as in Modules on Sites Sections 03CV and 093I

proof.text: The existing constant-scalar realization E has a natural tensor comparison E(M) tensor E(N) isomorphic to E(M tensor N). Curry its inverse and apply the existing total-bifunctor comparison. E is an equivalence and therefore preserves the coproducts forming total complexes, so this comparison is an isomorphism of total tensor complexes. Cancel E with canonical restriction using the explicit realization-restriction identity isomorphism and its fully-faithful cancellation counterpart. This gives rho(Tot(K tensor L)) isomorphic to Tot(rho K tensor rho L).

An additive equivalence reflects acyclicity: its homology comparison and faithfulness reflect the equality of the identity with zero. Lift any acyclic module-valued complex through the complex equivalence induced by rho and use the preceding total tensor comparison. The defining K-flatness of K proves acyclicity after tensoring with rho K. Symmetry gives the two tensor orders required by categorical K-flatness in the homotopy category. Thus rho K is categorically K-flat.

Apply the library K-flat derived-localization computation to rho K and rho M in degree zero. The single-complex functor commutes with termwise restriction, and total tensor with a single complex agrees with the termwise right-tensor complex. These isomorphisms, followed by the K-flat derived-localization comparison, give the required isomorphism for the fixed derived tensor.

theorem torModel_tensor_single_comparison
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (torModelRing Λ T)) ℤ)
    (hK : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := torModelCoefficientRing Λ T) K)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (torModelRing Λ T)) :
    let R : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (torModelRing Λ T) ⥤
      Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) := torModelRestriction Λ T
    let RC := R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    Nonempty (_root_.DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (RC.obj (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M) (curriedTensor _))) ≅
      (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) T).obj
        (_root_.DerivedCategory.Q.obj (RC.obj K))).obj
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (R.obj M))))
